_encyclopedia.Phobos:
Horizons: 401. The larger and closer of Mars's two moons, spiraling inward towards Mars.
Phobos is the larger and innermost of the two Martian satellites. It is a heavily cratered, low-density object that orbits closer 
to its parent planet than any other moon in the solar system.
Dimensions: It is a non-spherical, "triaxial" ellipsoid measuring approximately 26.0 x 22.8 x 18.2 km. Mean Radius: 11.1 km.
Mass: Approximately 1.0659 10^16 kg.
Density: It has a very low mean density of about 1.876 g/cm³, suggesting a porous "rubble pile" composition or a mix of rock and ice.
Surface Gravity: Extremely weak at 0.0057 m/s², meaning a person could easily jump off the surface into orbit.
Proximity: It orbits Mars at a mean distance of only 9,376 km from the planet's center (about 6,000 km from the surface).
Orbital Period: It completes one revolution every 7 hours and 39 minutes, meaning it orbits Mars three times in a single Martian day.
Tidal Locking: It is synchronously rotating, meaning the same face always points toward Mars.
Apparent Motion: Because it orbits faster than Mars rotates, it is the only moon that appears to rise in the West and set in the East.
Stickney Crater: Its most prominent feature is a massive impact crater nearly 9 km wide—large enough that the impact almost shattered the moon.
Orbital Decay: Phobos is below the "synchronous orbit" radius. Tidal forces are slowly dragging it closer to Mars at a rate of about 2 meters 
every 100 years. In roughly 30 to 50 million years, Phobos will either crash into Mars or be ripped apart by gravity to form a planetary ring.
Dust Rings: The moon is a source of seasonal dust rings around Mars as micrometeoroid impacts kick material off its surface.
Discovery: Found by Asaph Hall on August 18, 1877, just six days after he discovered the outer moon, Deimos.
Origin Theories: Scientists are still debating if Phobos is a captured carbonaceous asteroid from the main belt or formed from Martian impact debris.
Psyche Mission: On May 15, 2026 19:51 UTC the Psyche spacecraft will pass within 1,151 km of this moon.
_encyclopedia.Psyche:
Horizons:-255. JPL: "BACKGROUND:
Psyche is a NASA Discovery-class mission to map the surface and characterize
the composition of '16 Psyche', an elongated 280-km diameter metal-rich
asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. This
is the first mission to a metal-rich asteroid.

Psyche was launched Oct 13, 2023 @ 14:19:43 UTC on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy
from Kennedy Space Center, LC-39A.  Stage separation occurred 62 minutes
after launch at 15:21 UTC.

A gravity-assist flyby of Mars will occur in May 2026 at an altitude of
3000-4400 km above the surface, exact details depending on launch date.

The arrival phase ends June 26, 2029.
The asteroid's gravity will capture the spacecraft into orbit in late July
2029 and the two-year prime mission will begin in August. Psyche will
successively lower its orbit over the span of a year, eventually coming
as close as 75-km from the asteroid's surface.
